sara-support: Hey team — customer JD reports sudden spike in latency and a bunch of 401s for EU users since ~08:00 UTC. They say traffic is landing in us-west according to their logs. Can someone sanity-check routing?

customer-jd: Confirmed — our product metrics show p95 latency jumped from 120ms to 800ms for users in DE/FR. Auth logs show token verification failing because requests hit the us-west authorizer (different JWKS). We see requests with EU IPs but origin region header = us-west.

liam-eng: ugh. Do we have any recent rollout or config change for geo routing? I can glance at routing rules.

marta-netops: No infra rollouts this morning. Quick hypothesis: ISP resolver returning an out-of-date anycast answer or EDNS client-subnet being stripped. Any chance their ISP is doing resolver caching/sticky NAT?

customer-jd: We ran dig from their office and got US answers sometimes. Example: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 app.redwood.example A` returned 3.217.45.10 (us-west). But `dig +short @1.1.1.1` returned 18.194.2.5 (eu). TTLs are high (300s).

liam-eng: Can you paste a sample request trace (raw headers)? Need `x-redwood-pop` or our `via` header. Also any client IP seen in logs.

customer-jd: Pasting sanitized header from one failing request: ``
GET /v1/generate  HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
User-Agent: our-client/2.1
X-Forwarded-For: 81.2.69.10
X-Redwood-Pop: sea-us-west-2
Authorization: Bearer <token>
``
Note X-Redwood-Pop = sea-us-west-2 but client IP is in DE.

marta-netops: That is consistent with resolver returning us-west IP. Likely upstream resolver (ISP) cached an old A answer. Two things to check quickly: 1) GeoIP DB at edge — did we regress region mapping? 2) Did DNS zone TTL get increased accidentally?

liam-eng: Zone TTL is still 60 for health-balanced records. But our CDN also prefetches answers and could be serving from cache. ops-oncall, can you check edge resolver telemetry for an unusual surge of cache hits from some ASN ranges?

ops-oncall: Looking now — saw a big spike of queries from ASN 3320 between 07:50-08:10 UTC hitting our authoritative, and 78% of responses returned the us-west answer. Also seeing EDNS client-subnet flagged as empty for those queries.

sara-support: So ISP is stripping ECS and returning a sticky cached answer that points to us-west. That would explain cross-region auth fail and higher cost (longer egress). Customer is also seeing token mismatch because tokens are issued by eu authorizer.

liam-eng: Short-term mitigation options: 1) ask customer to enable DNS resolution via a resolver that supports ECS (not always possible) 2) Serve a short-lived redirect/cname that forces re-resolve 3) Push a low-ttl negative cache bust via rolling IP change on eu pool (risky). Thoughts?

marta-netops: We can also enable `geoip-heuristic-fallback` on the edge for that customer (force region by inspecting `X-Forwarded-For` and override pop). That requires a config change but is scoped per-tenant. Ops, any objections?

ops-oncall: We can flip a tenant-scoped routing override quickly. It will route by client IP rather than DNS answer for that tenant. Minimal risk. I'll prepare the change and a quick rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by ops-oncall for `tenant-routing-override` (changeset #7742). Will apply in ~2m.

customer-jd: Thank you — anything we can do on our side to help prevent reoccurrence?

sara-support: Recommend adding a fallback check in your client to detect high RTT and re-resolve DNS with a different public resolver, and to include `x-client-region` header when possible. We'll also follow up with our DNS provider about the spike and file support tickets with affected ISPs.

liam-eng: Follow-up tasks: - mesh with infra to confirm geoip DB current as of today (marta) - file ticket with DNS provider with pcaps and dig traces (sara) - add monitoring alert for asymmetric `X-Redwood-Pop` vs client IP region mismatches (liam)

marta-netops: GeoIP DB is current (2024-12-01). I'm investigating ASN 3320 queries; looks like an upstream cache flush happened but some resolvers kept stale entries until their TTL expired. I will escalate to DNS provider and request selective purge for the affected range.

ops-oncall: Override deployed. Customer reports initial success — p95 dropped back to ~130ms and auth 401s ceased for a subset of users. Leaving open to monitor for one hour then we'll rollback if stable.

customer-jd: Confirmed — metrics improving. Thanks everyone.

sara-support: I'll update the ticket and close after the hour if stable. Adding notes to billing: customer saw extra egress cost due to cross-region traffic; we'll evaluate credits once incident postmortem done. :+1:

liam-eng: For the postmortem, capture: root cause = upstream resolver cache + ECS stripped, contributing = TTL/edge prefetch behavior, mitigation = tenant routing override, long-term = better routing heuristics and detection alerts.

marta-netops: Filing DNS provider ticket now and attaching dig traces and ASN list.

ops-oncall: Monitoring dashboard shows rollback safe window at 09:45 UTC. Will coordinate with sara before flipping back.

sara-support: Great. Keeping thread pinned to ticket #INC-3387.
